Question: Which EC2 pricing model provides the LARGEST discount (up to 90%) in exchange for a 1- or 3-year commitment and partial upfront payment?
Explanation 1: On-Demand has no commitment, highest per-hour cost.
Explanation 2: Standard RIs provide up to 75% discount for 1- or 3-year commitment.
Explanation 3: Spot discounts are variable and based on spare capacity, up to ~90% off On-Demand.
Explanation 4: Dedicated Hosts are physical servers; you pay for the host, not the discount model.
Overall Explanation: Standard Reserved Instances provide up to 75% discount versus On-Demand for a 1- or 3-year commitment. Spot can be cheaper but is interruptible. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/

Question: Which Savings Plan type applies to EC2, Fargate, and Lambda usage, providing flexibility across instance families, regions, and sizes?
Explanation 1: EC2 Instance Savings Plans apply to EC2 only, but allow family/region changes.
Explanation 2: Compute Savings Plans apply to EC2, Fargate, and Lambda across families and regions.
Explanation 3: SageMaker Savings Plans apply to SageMaker only.
Explanation 4: No such Savings Plan type.
Overall Explanation: Compute Savings Plans offer the most flexibility, applying to EC2, Fargate, and Lambda. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/compute-pricing/

Question: Which EC2 pricing model is BEST for a fault-tolerant, flexible workload that can tolerate interruptions in exchange for the lowest price?
Explanation 1: On-Demand has the highest per-hour cost and no interruption risk.
Explanation 2: RIs require a 1- or 3-year commitment with no interruption.
Explanation 3: Spot provides up to 90% discount for interruptible fault-tolerant workloads.
Explanation 4: Dedicated Hosts are physical servers for licensing or compliance.
Overall Explanation: Spot Instances provide up to 90% discount for fault-tolerant workloads that can handle interruptions. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/spot/

Question: Which of the following are valid Reserved Instance attributes that affect pricing and billing? (Choose all that apply.)
Explanation 1: RI pricing varies by instance type.
Explanation 2: Regional RIs apply across sizes within a family.
Explanation 3: Tenancy affects RI pricing.
Explanation 4: Platform affects RI pricing and scope.
Overall Explanation: RI attributes include instance type, size, tenancy, platform, scope (region or AZ), and offering class. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/concepts-reserved-instances.html

Question: Which Reserved Instance class is the MOST flexible, allowing changes to instance type, family, OS, and tenancy?
Explanation 1: Standard RIs are the least flexible (instance size within family in same region).
Explanation 2: Convertible RIs allow changes to instance type, family, OS, and tenancy.
Explanation 3: Scheduled RIs run on a recurring schedule.
Explanation 4: Zonal RIs are scoped to a single AZ for capacity reservation.
Overall Explanation: Convertible RIs allow changes to instance type, OS, tenancy, and family during the term. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/convertible-reserved-instances.html

Question: What is the MAXIMUM term length for a Standard Reserved Instance?
Explanation 1: 1 year is the minimum term.
Explanation 2: 3 years is the maximum term, providing the largest discount.
Explanation 3: 5 years is not available for EC2 RIs.
Explanation 4: All RIs have a finite term.
Overall Explanation: Standard RIs are available for 1- or 3-year terms; 3 years gives the largest discount. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/reserved-instances/

Question: Which of the following are valid EC2 payment options for Reserved Instances? (Choose all that apply.)
Explanation 1: No Upfront has lowest discount, billed monthly.
Explanation 2: Partial Upfront balances upfront and monthly.
Explanation 3: All Upfront provides the largest discount.
Explanation 4: Pay-as-you-go is the On-Demand model, not RI.
Overall Explanation: RI payment options are No Upfront, Partial Upfront, and All Upfront, with All Upfront providing the largest discount. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/reserved-instances/

Question: What happens to the unused portion of a Reserved Instance when the matching instance is terminated?
Explanation 1: RIs cannot be refunded pro-rata.
Answer Option 2: It continues to apply to other matching instances in the same family
Explanation 2: Regional RIs automatically apply to other matching instances until exhausted.
Answer Option 3: It is converted to Savings Plans
Explanation 3: Unused RIs do not auto-convert to Savings Plans.
Explanation 4: No refund; RIs are consumed or applied to other instances.
Overall Explanation: Regional RIs apply to any matching instance in the region until the hour is consumed. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/apply_ri.html

Question: Which AWS pricing model provides a discount for a 1- or 3-year usage COMMITMENT measured in $/hour, applicable across instance families and regions?
Explanation 1: RIs commit to specific instance attributes, not just $/hour.
Explanation 2: Savings Plans commit to a $/hour spend and apply flexibly.
Explanation 3: Spot has no commitment.
Explanation 4: On-Demand has no discount or commitment.
Overall Explanation: Savings Plans commit to a $/hour spend and apply automatically to eligible usage across services. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/

Question: Which of the following are valid Savings Plan types? (Choose all that apply.)
Explanation 1: Compute Savings Plans apply to EC2, Fargate, and Lambda.
Explanation 2: EC2 Instance Savings Plans apply to EC2 in a family/region.
Explanation 3: SageMaker Savings Plans apply to SageMaker usage.
Explanation 4: There is no S3 Storage Savings Plan; S3 has its own pricing models.
Overall Explanation: Compute, EC2 Instance, and SageMaker are the three Savings Plan types. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/

Question: Which EC2 pricing model reserves CAPACITY for a specific instance type in a specific Availability Zone?
Explanation 1: On-Demand has no capacity reservation.
Explanation 2: Zonal RIs (scoped to a single AZ) reserve capacity for that instance type in that AZ.
Explanation 3: Regional RIs do not reserve capacity.
Explanation 4: Spot uses spare capacity, not reserved.
Overall Explanation: Zonal RIs reserve capacity for a specific instance type in a specific AZ, providing both discount and capacity assurance. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/concepts-reserved-instances.html

Question: Which EC2 feature lets you bid a maximum price for Spot Instances, with the Spot price fluctuating based on supply and demand?
Explanation 1: You set a max price; you pay the Spot market price, not your max, as long as it's below your max.
Explanation 2: Spot Fleet launches a mix of Spot and On-Demand.
Explanation 3: Spot block was discontinued; 'duration' replaces it.
Explanation 4: On-Demand has no bidding.
Overall Explanation: Set a max price for Spot; you pay the Spot market price, not your max, as long as Spot is below your max. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/using-spot-instances.html

Question: Which of the following workloads are BEST suited for Spot Instances? (Choose all that apply.)
Explanation 1: Batch jobs can be checkpointed and restarted.
Explanation 2: Stateless containers can be replaced.
Explanation 3: Build jobs are fault-tolerant and can be retried.
Explanation 4: Spot is not suited for stateful, latency-sensitive primaries.
Overall Explanation: Spot is suited for fault-tolerant, stateless, batch, container, and CI/CD workloads. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/spot/

Question: Which feature of EC2 Auto Scaling helps you reduce cost by terminating instances during predictable low-traffic periods?
Explanation 1: Scheduled scaling scales capacity at specific times, useful for predictable patterns.
Explanation 2: Target tracking reacts to a metric like CPU.
Explanation 3: Predictive scaling uses ML to forecast.
Explanation 4: Lifecycle hooks pause instance termination for custom actions.
Overall Explanation: Scheduled scaling scales capacity up or down at specific times, ideal for predictable patterns to reduce cost. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/schedule_time.html

Question: Which AWS tool recommends Reserved Instance purchases based on your historical On-Demand usage?
Explanation 1: Cost Explorer provides RI purchase recommendations based on past usage.
Explanation 2: Trusted Advisor provides checks including cost optimization.
Explanation 3: Budgets alerts on spend, not RI recommendations.
Explanation 4: Compute Optimizer recommends instance type rightsizing.
Overall Explanation: Cost Explorer RI recommendations suggest RIs based on your past On-Demand usage patterns. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/ce-ri-recommendations.html

Question: What is the maximum discount available for a 3-year Standard Reserved Instance with All Upfront payment?
Explanation 1: 1-year All Upfront provides up to 40%.
Explanation 2: 3-year No Upfront provides up to 60%.
Explanation 3: 3-year All Upfront provides the largest discount, up to 75%.
Explanation 4: Spot provides up to 90%.
Overall Explanation: 3-year Standard RIs with All Upfront provide up to 75% discount versus On-Demand. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/reserved-instances/

Question: Which of the following are valid Spot Instance interruption behaviors? (Choose all that apply.)
Explanation 1: Spot instances can be configured to stop on interruption.
Explanation 2: Spot instances can be configured to terminate on interruption.
Explanation 3: Spot instances can be configured to hibernate on interruption.
Explanation 4: Spot instances cannot auto-migrate.
Overall Explanation: Spot interruption behaviors are stop, terminate, or hibernate. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/spot-interruptions.html

Question: Which Spot feature lets you launch a portfolio of Spot and On-Demand instances with target capacity, automatically requesting resources to meet the target?
Explanation 1: Spot Fleet launches a mix of Spot and On-Demand to meet target capacity.
Explanation 2: Spot Instance is a single instance request.
Explanation 3: Auto Scaling uses launch templates, not Spot Fleet.
Explanation 4: RIs don't use Spot.
Overall Explanation: Spot Fleet launches a portfolio of instance types and purchasing models to meet target capacity at the lowest price. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/spot-fleet.html

Question: Which AWS service provides a serverless, pay-per-request compute model with no charge when idle, billed in 1 ms increments?
Explanation 1: EC2 bills per second/hour, with minimum charges.
Explanation 2: Lambda bills per request and GB-second, no charge when idle.
Explanation 3: ECS is a container orchestrator; you pay for underlying compute.
Explanation 4: EKS bills per cluster hour plus underlying compute.
Overall Explanation: AWS Lambda is the most cost-efficient compute for variable workloads, with no charge when idle and 1 ms billing. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/lambda/pricing/

Question: Which EC2 feature lets you set a HOURLY budget that, when exceeded, automatically stops the instance to prevent runaway costs?
Explanation 1: Interruption behavior is for Spot, not budget.
Explanation 2: Auto Scaling does not have a budget feature.
Explanation 3: Use AWS Budgets with a stop action on an alarm, or third-party tools.
Explanation 4: Lambda does not have this feature for EC2.
Overall Explanation: Use AWS Budgets with an alarm and a stop action (via CloudWatch + Lambda) to stop instances when budget is exceeded. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/budgets-managing-costs.html

Question: Which of the following are valid benefits of Compute Savings Plans over EC2 Instance Savings Plans? (Choose all that apply.)
Explanation 1: Compute Savings Plans apply to EC2, Fargate, and Lambda.
Explanation 2: Compute Savings Plans apply to any family.
Explanation 3: Compute Savings Plans apply across regions.
Explanation 4: EC2 Instance Savings Plans provide the same or slightly higher discount but less flexibility.
Overall Explanation: Compute Savings Plans offer the most flexibility (EC2, Fargate, Lambda, any family, any region) versus EC2 Instance Savings Plans. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/compute-pricing/

Question: Which AWS feature provides automatic discounts on S3 storage as your usage grows, with no commitment required?
Explanation 1: Intelligent-Tiering auto-tiers but does not provide a volume discount per se.
Explanation 2: S3 has tiered pricing where per-GB cost decreases as usage grows.
Explanation 3: There is no S3 Reserved Capacity; S3 Glacier has Reserved Capacity.
Explanation 4: Standard-IA has a lower per-GB rate but retrieval fees.
Overall Explanation: S3 has tiered pricing where the per-GB cost decreases as your storage volume grows, with no commitment. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/s3/pricing/

Question: Which S3 storage class is the LOWEST cost for long-term archives where retrieval time of 12 hours is acceptable?
Explanation 1: Glacier Instant Retrieval is millisecond retrieval.
Explanation 2: Glacier Flexible Retrieval supports minutes to hours.
Explanation 3: Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost class, with 12-hour retrieval.
Explanation 4: Standard-IA is for infrequent access, not archive.
Overall Explanation: S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost S3 storage class for 7-10 year archives with 12-hour retrieval. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/s3/storage-classes/

Question: Which S3 storage class is the BEST fit for data accessed less than once a quarter, with millisecond retrieval and no retrieval fees?
Explanation 1: Standard is for frequent access, not cost-optimized for rare access.
Explanation 2: Standard-IA has retrieval fees and per-GB retrieval charges.
Explanation 3: Glacier Instant Retrieval provides millisecond retrieval with no retrieval fees for quarterly access.
Explanation 4: Glacier Flexible has minutes-to-hours retrieval, not millisecond.
Overall Explanation: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval provides millisecond retrieval with no retrieval fees, ideal for quarterly access. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/s3/storage-classes/

Question: Which S3 storage class automatically moves objects to the most cost-effective access tier based on changing access patterns, with no operational overhead?
Explanation 1: Standard is a fixed tier, not auto-tiering.
Explanation 2: Intelligent-Tiering auto-tiers based on access patterns.
Explanation 3: Glacier Deep Archive is a fixed tier.
Explanation 4: One Zone-IA is a fixed tier for single-AZ infrequent access.
Overall Explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering auto-tiers objects across access tiers based on access patterns with no operational overhead. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/intelligent-tiering.html

Question: Which of the following are valid S3 lifecycle transition targets? (Choose all that apply.)
Explanation 1: Lifecycle can transition to Standard-IA.
Explanation 2: Lifecycle can transition to One Zone-IA.
Explanation 3: Lifecycle can transition to Glacier Instant Retrieval.
Explanation 4: Lifecycle can transition to Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
Overall Explanation: Lifecycle can transition objects to Standard-IA, One Zone-IA, Glacier Instant Retrieval, Glacier Flexible Retrieval, and Glacier Deep Archive. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lifecycle-mgmt.html

Question: Which S3 storage class is the MOST cost-effective for data that can be recreated, with single-AZ availability and infrequent access?
Explanation 1: Standard is multi-AZ, more expensive.
Explanation 2: Standard-IA is multi-AZ with retrieval fees.
Explanation 3: One Zone-IA stores in a single AZ, 20% cheaper than Standard-IA, for reproducible data.
Explanation 4: Glacier is for archive with retrieval delays.
Overall Explanation: S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ, with 20% lower cost than Standard-IA, for reproducible infrequent data. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/s3/storage-classes/

Question: Which S3 Glacier retrieval option provides the FASTEST access (1-5 minutes) but at a higher cost than Standard retrieval?
Explanation 1: Standard is the slowest, cheapest Flexible retrieval.
Explanation 2: Expedited retrieval is 1-5 minutes, higher cost.
Explanation 3: Bulk is the cheapest, slowest Flexible retrieval.
Explanation 4: S3 Standard is not a Glacier option.
Overall Explanation: Glacier Flexible Retrieval offers Standard (3-5h), Bulk (5-12h), and Expedited (1-5 min) tiers. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/s3/storage-classes/

Question: Which S3 feature lets you reduce storage cost by automatically deleting incomplete multipart uploads that were never completed?
Explanation 1: Lifecycle can abort incomplete multipart uploads.
Explanation 2: Replication copies objects, not aborts uploads.
Explanation 3: Event Notifications are for downstream actions, not aborts.
Explanation 4: Object Lock is for WORM, not upload cleanup.
Overall Explanation: Use S3 Lifecycle with the AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload action to clean up incomplete multipart uploads. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/mpu-abort-incomplete-mpu.html

Question: Which of the following are valid S3 cost optimization techniques? (Choose all that apply.)
Answer Option 1: Lifecycle policies to transition to cheaper tiers
Explanation 1: Lifecycle transitions reduce cost.
Answer Option 2: S3 Intelligent-Tiering for unknown access patterns
Explanation 2: Intelligent-Tiering auto-optimizes cost.
Explanation 3: Object Lock is for compliance, not cost optimization.
Answer Option 4: S3 Lifecycle to expire (delete) old versions
Explanation 4: Expiring old noncurrent versions reduces cost.
Overall Explanation: Lifecycle transitions, Intelligent-Tiering, and expiring old noncurrent versions reduce S3 cost. Object Lock is for compliance. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-cost-optimization.html

Question: Which S3 Glacier pricing model provides a LOWER per-GB-month cost in exchange for committing to a fixed provisioned capacity unit?
Explanation 1: On-Demand is the default with no commitment.
Explanation 2: Glacier Reserved Capacity provides a discount in exchange for a capacity commitment.
Explanation 3: S3 Standard is not a Glacier class.
Explanation 4: Glacier Instant Retrieval is a separate class, not a pricing model.
Overall Explanation: S3 Glacier Reserved Capacity provides a discount in exchange for committing to a provisioned capacity. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/s3/glacier/pricing/

Question: Which S3 storage class provides millisecond retrieval, single AZ storage, and is 20% cheaper than S3 Standard-IA?
Explanation 1: One Zone-IA is single-AZ, 20% cheaper than Standard-IA, millisecond retrieval.
Explanation 2: Standard-IA is multi-AZ.
Explanation 3: Glacier Instant Retrieval is multi-AZ.
Explanation 4: Standard is multi-AZ and more expensive.
Overall Explanation: S3 One Zone-IA is single-AZ, millisecond retrieval, 20% cheaper than Standard-IA. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/s3/storage-classes/

Question: Which S3 request type is FREE for the request itself but charged per GB transferred out?
Explanation 1: PUT requests are charged per 1,000 requests.
Explanation 2: Cross-region GETs are charged per 1,000 + per GB transfer.
Explanation 3: Data transfer out to internet is charged per GB, with no per-request fee.
Explanation 4: Lifecycle transitions are charged per 1,000 objects.
Overall Explanation: Data transfer out to internet is charged per GB, with no per-request fee. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/s3/pricing/

Question: Which S3 feature lets you replicate objects to a destination bucket in another region, useful for DR and reducing latency?
Explanation 1: CRR replicates objects to a bucket in another region.
Explanation 2: SRR replicates within the same region.
Explanation 3: Transfer Acceleration is for faster uploads, not replication.
Explanation 4: Multi-Region Access Point provides a single global endpoint over replicated buckets.
Overall Explanation: S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) replicates objects to a destination bucket in another region. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html

Question: Which S3 pricing factor is FREE for the first 100 GB per month, with no charge?
Explanation 1: Storage is not free.
Explanation 2: Data transfer out to internet is free for the first 100 GB per month.
Explanation 3: PUT requests are not free.
Explanation 4: Replication has per-GB and per-request charges.
Overall Explanation: Data transfer out to internet is free for the first 100 GB per month. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/s3/pricing/

Question: Which S3 feature lets you STORE and QUERY data directly without retrieving the full object, reducing data transfer cost?
Explanation 1: S3 Select queries a subset of data server-side, reducing data transfer.
Explanation 2: Glacier Select queries archive objects server-side.
Explanation 3: S3 Inventory lists objects, doesn't query data.
Explanation 4: Batch Operations performs bulk actions on objects.
Overall Explanation: S3 Select and S3 Glacier Select query a subset of data server-side, reducing data transfer and cost. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/selecting-content-from-objects.html

Question: Which of the following are valid S3 storage classes that support S3 Object Lock for WORM (Write Once Read Many) compliance? (Choose all that apply.)
Explanation 1: Standard supports Object Lock.
Explanation 2: Standard-IA supports Object Lock.
Explanation 3: Glacier Flexible Retrieval supports Object Lock.
Explanation 4: One Zone-IA supports Object Lock.
Overall Explanation: Object Lock is supported on Standard, Standard-IA, One Zone-IA, Glacier Instant, Glacier Flexible, and Deep Archive. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock.html

Question: Which S3 storage class is the BEST choice for backups of on-premises databases, with 12-hour retrieval tolerance and the lowest storage cost?
Explanation 1: Standard is for frequent access, not cost-optimized for backups.
Explanation 2: Glacier Flexible supports 1-5 min to 12 hours, not the lowest cost.
Explanation 3: Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost class with 12-hour retrieval, ideal for backups.
Explanation 4: One Zone-IA is for infrequent access, not the lowest cost for backups.
Overall Explanation: S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost class with 12-hour retrieval, ideal for backups and long-term archives. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/s3/storage-classes/

Question: Which EBS volume type is the LEAST EXPENSIVE per GB for COLD, infrequently accessed data with the lowest storage cost?
Explanation 1: gp3 is general-purpose SSD.
Explanation 2: io2 is the highest-performance SSD, most expensive per GB.
Explanation 3: st1 is throughput-optimized HDD.
Explanation 4: EBS sc1 is the lowest-cost HDD, for cold data.
Overall Explanation: EBS sc1 is the lowest-cost EBS volume type for cold, infrequently accessed data. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/ebs/pricing/

Question: Which EBS volume type is the LEAST EXPENSIVE per GB for FREQUENTLY accessed, throughput-intensive workloads?
Explanation 1: gp3 is general-purpose SSD with predictable IOPS.
Explanation 2: io2 is high-performance, more expensive.
Explanation 3: EBS st1 is the lowest-cost HDD, optimized for throughput-intensive workloads.
Explanation 4: sc1 is cold HDD, lower throughput than st1.
Overall Explanation: EBS st1 is throughput-optimized HDD, lowest cost per GB for throughput-intensive workloads like big data. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/ebs/volume-types/

Question: Which feature of gp3 EBS volumes lets you provision IOPS and throughput INDEPENDENTLY of volume size, reducing cost for performance-driven workloads?
Explanation 1: io1 is a separate volume type.
Explanation 2: gp3 allows independent provisioning of IOPS and throughput from size.
Explanation 3: Multi-Attach is for shared volumes, not performance.
Explanation 4: Snapshots are backups, not performance.
Overall Explanation: gp3 EBS volumes decouple IOPS and throughput from size, allowing right-sized performance at lower cost. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/ebs/volume-types/

Question: Which of the following are valid strategies to REDUCE EBS cost? (Choose all that apply.)
Explanation 1: Match volume type and size to workload needs.
Explanation 2: gp3 is 20% cheaper than gp2 at baseline.
Explanation 3: Orphaned volumes incur charges; delete or snapshot.
Explanation 4: Over-provisioning volumes wastes cost.
Overall Explanation: Right-size volume type, use gp3 over gp2, and delete unused volumes to reduce EBS cost. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/ebs/pricing/

Question: Which AWS service provides RECOMMENDATIONS to right-size EBS volumes based on utilization metrics?
Explanation 1: Cost Explorer shows spend, not rightsizing recs.
Explanation 2: Compute Optimizer recommends right-sizing for EC2, EBS, and Lambda.
Explanation 3: Trusted Advisor provides cost checks, not detailed EBS rightsizing.
Explanation 4: Budgets alerts on spend, not rightsizing.
Overall Explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer recommends right-sizing for EC2 instances, EBS volumes, and Lambda functions based on CloudWatch metrics. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/what-is.html

Question: Which storage option provides TEMPORARY, instance-local storage that is FREE (no additional charge) but DATA IS LOST on stop, terminate, or hardware failure?
Explanation 1: EBS is network-attached and persists independently.
Explanation 2: Instance store is local, free, but data is lost on stop/terminate/hardware failure.
Explanation 3: EFS is a network file system with a per-GB charge.
Explanation 4: FSx is a managed file system with a per-GB charge.
Overall Explanation: Instance store is local NVMe/SSD storage included in the instance price, free, but data is lost on stop/terminate/hardware failure. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/InstanceStorage.html

Question: Which EBS snapshot pricing factor is FREE for the first 100 GB per month?
Explanation 1: Snapshot storage is not free; first 100 GB of standard tier is free.
Explanation 2: Snapshot data transfer out is not free in general.
Explanation 3: FSR is charged per snapshot per AZ per month.
Explanation 4: Cross-region copy is charged per GB.
Overall Explanation: EBS snapshot storage is free for the first 100 GB per month under the standard tier. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/ebs/pricing/

Question: Which EBS snapshot tier provides the LOWEST cost per GB-month for long-term archive snapshots?
Explanation 1: Standard is the default tier.
Explanation 2: EBS Archive tier provides the lowest cost for snapshots accessed less than once a quarter.
Explanation 3: There is no Cold tier; Archive is the lower tier.
Explanation 4: EBS snapshots integrate with S3 Glacier Deep Archive via Archive tier.
Overall Explanation: EBS Snapshot Archive tier provides up to 75% lower cost for snapshots accessed less than once a quarter. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-archive.html

Question: Which of the following are valid cost optimization strategies for EC2 instance storage? (Choose all that apply.)
Answer Option 1: Use instance store for temporary data
Explanation 1: Instance store is free, ideal for temp/buffer data.
Explanation 2: Match volume type to workload to avoid overpaying.
Explanation 3: Orphaned volumes still cost money.
Answer Option 4: Use larger EBS volumes for all workloads
Explanation 4: Larger volumes cost more; size appropriately.
Overall Explanation: Use instance store for temp data, right-size EBS volumes, and delete unused volumes to optimize cost. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/ebs/pricing/

Question: Which EBS feature lets you modify volume type, size, and IOPS WITHOUT restarting the instance, reducing operational overhead and cost?
Explanation 1: Snapshots require creating a new volume.
Explanation 2: Multi-Attach is for shared volumes.
Explanation 3: Elastic Volumes allow modification without restart.
Explanation 4: Encryption does not affect modification.
Overall Explanation: EBS Elastic Volumes allow modification of type, size, and IOPS without restart, reducing operational overhead. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/evs.html

Question: Which AWS tool analyzes your past 14 days of CloudWatch metrics and recommends EC2 instance type rightsizing to reduce cost?
Explanation 1: Cost Explorer shows spend trends.
Explanation 2: Compute Optimizer recommends rightsizing based on CloudWatch metrics.
Explanation 3: Trusted Advisor provides checks.
Explanation 4: Systems Manager is for ops automation.
Overall Explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer recommends EC2, EBS, and Lambda rightsizing based on 14 days of CloudWatch metrics. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/what-is.html

Question: Which feature of Amazon EFS provides a LOWER per-GB cost for files NOT accessed for 30+ days, while remaining available?
Explanation 1: EFS Standard is the default tier.
Explanation 2: EFS IA provides a lower per-GB cost for files not accessed for 30+ days.
Explanation 3: EFS Archive provides even lower cost for files not accessed for 90+ days.
Explanation 4: There is no EFS Cold tier.
Overall Explanation: EFS Infrequent Access (IA) provides a lower per-GB cost for files not accessed for 30+ days, with EFS Lifecycle moving them automatically. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/lifecycle-management-efs.html

Question: Which AWS Lambda feature provides a discount of up to 17% for a 1- or 3-year commit, in exchange for predictable usage?
Explanation 1: SnapStart reduces cold starts, not pricing.
Explanation 2: Lambda usage is covered by Compute Savings Plans for up to 17% discount.
Explanation 3: Reserved Concurrency is a throttling feature.
Explanation 4: Provisioned Concurrency is for latency-sensitive workloads.
Overall Explanation: Lambda is eligible for Compute Savings Plans, providing up to 17% discount for 1- or 3-year commits. Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/lambda/pricing/

Question: Which AWS Lambda feature provides INIT environments to keep functions warm, reducing cold start latency at additional cost?
Explanation 1: SnapStart caches initialized environments, reducing cold starts at no extra cost.
Explanation 2: Provisioned Concurrency keeps functions initialized at additional cost.
Explanation 3: Layers are for code sharing.
Explanation 4: Event Source Mappings are for triggers.
Overall Explanation: Provisioned Concurrency keeps functions initialized for low-latency at an additional cost. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/provisioned-concurrency.html

Question: Which AWS service is the MOST cost-effective for running containers with VARIABLE, bursty workloads that can scale to zero?
